title: Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere
main_claim: For every prime p, height n>=1 and integer t, pi_t L_{K(n)} S_p^ is a finitely generated Z_p-module. This is equivalent to the same statement for any finite p-local spectrum. The proof goes through finiteness of H^a_cts(P_n; (E_n)_{2t}/p) for a larger class of division-tuple coefficients, proved by downward induction on height strata. Each step shows open-stratum countability (via Cartier transfers and a residue/Laurent model) and then uses the fact that a compact, countable Hausdorff group is finite.
coverage:
I read these in full and checked them line by line:
- sec 1 (introduction and outline).
- sec 12 (descent spectral sequence for S/p with a horizontal vanishing line, the derived-completeness / Milnor / compact-Nakayama lemma, the ranks corollary against BSSW, and the height-one calculation, including v_p((1+p)^t-1)=1+v_p(t)).
- sec 11 (the height induction, finite marking descent via the Amitsur/H-cochain double complex, the m=1 and m>1 representation reductions, the strip/colimit boundary comparison, and the corollary for the extended stabilizer).
- sec 10 (the tail category A mod countable spaces, pro-constant lemma, exact pro-completion with Artin-Rees, uniform image stabilization by descending induction, the top Koszul edge-map argument and spectral-sequence differential elimination, the finite forgetting-kernel lemma, the fixed boundary operator, and the m>1 and m=1 contradiction/splitting arguments).
- sec 9 (pole recurrence and lattice choice, which I checked arithmetically; the residue quotient W/W_+ ~= Q; Frobenius contraction plus the Baire/Pettis analytic-subgroup argument for acyclicity of W_+; finiteness of the stable transfer image; the compact-operator lemma; and the localized-intersection proposition).
- prop:cts-isotropy-bound, lem:cts-local-section and prop:mark-finite-isotropy (free action of finite subgroups on marked open covers, trace-one elements).
- lem:ind-admissible-cohomology, cor:ind-finite and cor:laurent-finite (phi-fixed points and duality).

Each step in these parts held up. The degree count also matches: the root cover B^{1/q^{m-1}} has degree q^d over B, consistent with dim Lambda_q = q^d.

Not verified in detail: the geometric sections 4-8. These are the completed-tower identification with independent tuples in H^1(O(-1/m)) on the relative Fargues-Fontaine curve, the uniform Kummer support calculations, thm:ind-comparison, the existence and normalization of the invariant volume and Cartier transfer (prop:trans-volume, prop:trans-cartier, prop:trans-roots), and the Laurent support comparison. The whole result rests on these unchecked inputs, so the verdict is no gap found in what was audited, not a confirmation of the theorem.
